title: Ahmad ibn Fadlan
summary: Ahmad ibn Fadlan was a tenth-century Arab scholar and official envoy dispatched from Abbasid Baghdad in 921 to the ruler of the Volga Bulgars. His surviving travelogue, the Risala, provides an invaluable firsthand ethnographic account of the Volga Bulgars, the nomadic Turkic peoples of Central Asia, and the Scandinavian Rus traders, including a famous eyewitness description of a Viking ship funeral.

uncertainty.note: Journey began in 921 and lasted three and a half years; exact birth and death dates are unknown.
